events.what: UKMTO reports 12 ships attacked in or near Hormuz in past seven days; IRGC says a tanker on fire in Sea of Oman after trying to transit a 'restricted area'
IEA Governing Board to accelerate emergency stock release, incl. over 20 million barrels diesel; total draw to exceed 400 million-barrel pledge
Two tankers caught fire off Romania amid drone attacks; Black Sea crude war risk premium at $4.60/b, highest since assessment began Oct 2022
US Energy Secretary Wright signalled possible relaxation of sanctions on shadow-fleet tankers to curb freight costs
30-day deadline under Sept. 18 Russian oil sanctions law for administration to impose sanctions (waivers allowed; tariffs up to 100%)
US Treasury waiver allows sale and import of Russian diesel until April 7, 2027; Russia partially lifts diesel export ban Oct. 10
US extends Lukoil international waivers (filling stations, Bulgarian assets) to April 24, 2027
Explosion on al-Jabsah gas pipeline and sabotage on Banias-Homs products pipeline; oil pipeline in al-Hasakah attacked Oct. 7
Iraq hands Kirkuk, Bai Hassan, Khabbaz and Jambur fields to BP, targeting 450,000 b/d
Houthi 'maritime embargo' on Saudi Arabia; two Saudi-linked ships still crossed Bab al-Mandab
Japanese Cabinet approved bill giving grants for crude/product purchases from suppliers outside Hormuz

themes.summary: Twelve ship attacks near Hormuz in a week, Middle East crude exports at 11.9 million b/d in October vs 15 million b/d in September, and ICE Brent at $109.86/b, highest since May 19.

themes.theme: Record freight and tanker sanctions relief

IEA to accelerate emergency release, about 330 million barrels released so far and total to exceed 400 million, including over 20 million barrels diesel.

themes.theme: Russia diesel, sanctions and Ukraine strikes
themes.summary: US waiver and Russian partial diesel ban lifting, new sanctions law deadline Oct. 18, Black Sea war risk at $4.60/b and Ukrainian strikes idling almost half of Russian primary refining.
China unlikely to refill reserves without sharp price drop; stocks at 1.242 billion barrels as of Oct. 15; September imports 9.06 million b/d.
Dubai time spread $2.69/b (from $3.695/b) and Dated Brent $125.975/b on Oct. 15 vs peak $144.42/b on Apr. 7.
